content: Their daughter Ana is 45, a nurse, and calls every Sunday evening.
Their son Marc lives in Manchester with his wife Claire.
Ana's children are Lucía, 12, and Pau, 8.
Their husband Jordi died in 2023; they were married for 48 years.
They live alone in a second-floor flat on Carrer de Verdi in Gràcia, Barcelona.
Their neighbour Montse in flat 2B has a spare key and checks in most mornings.
They take donepezil 5 mg every morning with breakfast.
They take amlodipine for blood pressure at 8 pm.
They were diagnosed with early-stage Alzheimer's in January 2026.
Their GP is Dr. Patel at the CAP Vila de Gràcia health centre.
They see the neurologist Dr. Serra at Hospital Sant Pau every three months.
They are allergic to penicillin.
They walk to Plaça de la Virreina every morning at about 10.
They go to the lunch club at the community centre on Tuesdays and Thursdays.
Their cat is called Mixa, a grey tabby, and eats twice a day.
Their brother Leo lives in Porto.
Their brother Leo moved from Porto to Lisbon in March 2026.
Leo's birthday is on 14 June.
A carer called Sílvia comes on Monday mornings to help with shopping.
Their carer is now Núria, who comes on Monday and Friday mornings; Sílvia left in September.
They used to sing in the Orfeó Gracienc choir and still love Catalan folk songs.
They play the old upright piano in the living room, mostly Granados.
They were a primary school teacher at Escola Fructuós Gelabert for 35 years.
Their signature dish is Jordi's mother's fideuà, made for family Sundays.
They can't stand coriander.
They drink a cortado with oat milk in the afternoons.
They are planning to visit Marc in Manchester for Christmas, flying on 20 December.
They wear a hearing aid in the left ear and the batteries are size 312.
They keep their reading glasses in the blue case on the kitchen shelf.
They keep the house keys on the hook by the front door, next to the umbrella.
Ana's mobile number is saved in the phone under 'Ana filla'.
Their bank branch is the CaixaBank on Gran de Gràcia; Ana helps with paperwork.
Their oldest friend Carme lives in Sant Cugat and phones on Wednesdays.
Carme had a hip replacement in October and is recovering at home.
They grow tomatoes and basil in pots on the balcony.
They watch the TV3 news at 9 pm every night.
Their wedding anniversary with Jordi was 22 May; it is a hard day each year.
Jordi is buried at Montjuïc cemetery and they visit with Ana on his birthday, 3 November.
They sleep badly when it is too warm and use a small fan in summer.
Ana set up a big-button tablet for video calls.
Lucía started secondary school this year and is learning the violin.
Pau plays football for a youth team on Saturday mornings.
They had a fall in the bathroom in August, so there is now a grab rail by the bath.
In an emergency they should press the red Creu Roja alarm pendant they wear.
They go to Mass at Sant Joan de Gràcia on some Sundays.
